extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, judges, and legal scholars handling re-issue/amendment of patents
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for when and how an issued patent may be re-issued or amended without impermissibly enlarging or changing the original invention; guidance on joinder of process, apparatus, product, manufacture, composition, design, and improvements in re-issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of machine limited to same parts or equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: The re-issue of a patent for a machine must be limited to the same parts or their equivalents associated under the same structural law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "The re-issue of a patent for a machine, if the machine be not a combination, must be limited to the same parts or their equivalents associated under the same structural law." Examples/cases cited throughout §675 support this limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may vary in mechanical adaptation and cover modes of use previously indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue may vary from the original in matters of mechanical adaptation, and may cover any mode of using the machine which has been properly indicated in the former specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "The re-issue may vary from the original in matters of mechanical adaptation, and may cover any mode of using the machine which has been properly indicated in the former specification." Cases cited: Tucker v. Tucker Mfg. Co., Morris v. Boyer, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of combination may embrace suggested elements and sub-combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When the machine is a combination, the re-issue may embrace such of its elements and sub-combinations as are suggested in the original description, if not abandoned or disclaimed, and if due to the inventive genius of the same inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "When the machine is a combination, the re-issue may embrace such of its elements and sub-combinations as are suggested in the original description, if not abandoned or disclaimed, and if due to the inventive genius of the same inventor."

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine patent cannot be re-issued to include mere-use processes
rubrics_metrics.description: A machine-patent cannot be re-issued to include a process which consists in the mere use of the machine, nor a process in which the patented machine performs a necessary though subordinate part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "A machine-patent cannot, however, be re-issued to include a process which consists in the mere use of the machine, nor a process in which the patented machine performs a necessary though subordinate part." Explanation: the function of the machine is protected by the machine patent, but the process itself is distinct and not patentable as part of the machine re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and apparatus inseparably connected may be joined
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the process cannot be performed without the apparatus mentioned, or the product uniformly follows the employment of the process, the inventions are inseparably connected and product or apparatus may be covered by a re-issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (earlier paragraph): "Thus where the process cannot be performed without the apparatus mentioned, or the product uniformly follows the employment of the process, the inventions are inseparably connected with each other, and the product or the apparatus may be covered by a re-issue of the patent for the art." Case examples: Powder Works, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of process may omit described steps if substantially same
rubrics_metrics.description: The re-issue of a patent for a process may omit some of the steps described in the original, if the process remains substantially the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That the re-issue of a patent for a process may omit some of the steps described in the original, if the process remains substantially the same," with cases such as Ex parte Wooten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot add a new step to a process
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue of a patent for a process cannot add a new step to that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That a re-issue of a patent for a process cannot add a new step," with citation American Middlings Purifier Co. v. Atlantic Milling Co. (1879).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue for product void when original limited to process (unless product inevitably results)
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue of a patent for a product is void where the original was for the process unless the use of the process always results in the product so that the inventions are essentially the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That a re-issue of a patent for a product is void, where the original was for the process, unless the use of the process always results in the product, and thus both are one invention;" examples and cases cited (e.g., Powder Co. v. Powder Works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original patent confined to product by single process cannot re-issue to all modes of making product
rubrics_metrics.description: An original patent confined to a product produced by one process only cannot re-issue to cover the product however produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That an original patent confined to a product produced by one process only cannot re-issue to cover the product, however produced," with citation Tacuum Oil Co. v. Buffalo Lubricating Oil Co. (1884).

rubrics_metrics.name: If original describes both process and product but claims process only, re-issue may cover product
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the original describes both process and product, but claims only the process, the patent may re-issue to cover the product also.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That where the original described both process and product, but claims the process only, it may re-issue to cover the product also," with cases Tucker v. Duna (1881) and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of machine may claim inseparably connected product
rubrics_metrics.description: The product of a machine, if inseparably connected with it and otherwise within the rule of joinder, may also be claimed in the re-issue of the machine patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "The product of a machine, if inseparably connected with it and otherwise within the rule of joinder so often stated, may also be claimed in the re-issue." See §675 notes and cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of manufacture limited to same concrete instrument or dependent inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An original patent for a manufacture can be re-issued only for the same concrete instrument, or for inventions upon which the production of such manufacture may depend; essential characteristics attributed in original must be found in re-issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (§676): "Whatever essential characteristics have been attributed to the manufacture in the original specification must be found in it as described and claimed in the re-issue; and ... the identity of the invention must be distinctly traceable."

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot ascribe manufacture to different processes or altered properties
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manufacture was first described as resulting from certain processes and possessing certain properties, the re-issue cannot depart from this delineation by ascribing it to different processes or attributing other properties due to changes in mode of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "the re-issue cannot depart from this delineation by ascribing it to different processes, or attributing to it other properties due to changes in the mode by which it is produced." Cases cited: Cochrane v. Anilin, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue may disclose new methods of applying a manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: New methods of applying a manufacture to practical use or new connections in which it may be employed can be disclosed in the re-issue, since these involve no alteration in the nature of the invention itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "But new methods of applying it to practical use or new connections in which it may be employed can be disclosed, since these involve no alteration in the nature of the invention itself."

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot claim an article in any form if original limited to particular form
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original patent was for an article in a particular form, a re-issue claiming it under whatever form is void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That where an original patent was for an article in a particular form, a re-issue claiming it under whatever form is void," with case Campbell v. Kavanagh (1882).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue for a composition limited to same or equivalent ingredients and modes
rubrics_metrics.description: A composition patent can re-issue only for the same or equivalent ingredients, united by the same or equivalent modes of intermixture, resulting in a compound possessing the same or equivalent properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (§677): "A composition of matter ... can re-issue only for the same or equivalent ingredients, united by the same or equivalent modes of intermixture, and resulting in a compound possessing the same or equivalent properties."

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-ingredients described originally may be omitted or others added
rubrics_metrics.description: Substances which are not ingredients, though described in the original as entering into the composition, may be omitted or others may be added without disturbing identity; variations in intermixture not altering substantial character are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "Substances which are not ingredients ... may be omitted or others may be added without disturbing the identity of the invention, and variations in the mode of intermixture, which do not alter its substantial character, may be introduced."

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovered ingredients/sub-combinations may be claimed if inventor's and not public
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original has sufficiently indicated the nature of the several ingredients or their sub-combinations, these may be claimed in the re-issue if they were discovered by the inventor and have not already passed into the possession of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "When the original has sufficiently indicated the nature of the several ingredients, or of their sub-combinations, these may also be claimed in the re-issue if they were discovered by the inventor ... and have not already passed from his control into the possession of the public."

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts or instruments necessarily employed may be joined with composition if suggested originally
rubrics_metrics.description: Arts or instruments invented by the same inventor and necessarily employed in manufacturing the composition may be joined with it in the re-issue when their essential attributes were suggested in the original patent and they have neither been abandoned nor disclaimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "All arts or instruments invented by the same inventor and necessarily employed in manufacturing the composition, may be joined with it in the re-issue when their essential attributes were suggested in the original patent and they have neither been abandoned nor disclaimed."

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrinsic matters (packing/uses on sale) cannot be inserted in composition patent
rubrics_metrics.description: No extrinsic matter, such as a mode of packing the compound when completed, or of using it for practical purposes when sold, can be inserted in the patent for the composition either originally or by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "But no extrinsic matter, such as a mode of packing the compound when completed, or of using it for practical purposes when sold, can be inserted in the patent for the composition either originally or by amendment." Explanation: these are patentable inventions but not joinable where composition is principal invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of design confined to design described or suggested originally
rubrics_metrics.description: The re-issue of a design-patent must be confined to the design described or suggested in the original specification; identity is determined by appearance to the eye and characteristic features must be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (§678): "The re-issue of a design-patent must be confined to the design described or suggested in the original specification. The identity of the design is determined by the appearance which it presents to the eye ..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements/sub-combinations of design may be claimed if they answer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements and sub-combinations of the original design, if answering the stated requirements, may be claimed in the re-issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "The elements and sub-combinations of the original design, if answering the requirements already mentioned, may be claimed in the re-issue;" see §§477, 588 notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design re-issue cannot embrace distinct manufacture invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the same article is both a new design and a new manufacture, the inventions are distinct and independent, and a re-issue of a patent for it as one cannot embrace the article considered as the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "where the same article is both a new design and a new manufacture, the inventions are distinct and independent, and a re-issue of a patent for it as the one cannot embrace the article considered as the other."

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of improvement confined to exact improvement suggested originally
rubrics_metrics.description: An improvement is subordinate to an existing art and the re-issue must be confined to the exact improvement suggested or described in the original patent; it may include processes or implements producing the improvement but not arts/instruments occupying relations of function or effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (§679): "The re-issue must be confined to the exact improvement, suggested or described in the original patent. It may include processes or implements by which the improvement is produced. It cannot embrace arts or instruments which occupy toward the improvement the relation of either functions or effects."

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot embrace matter previously or impliedly excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issued patent cannot embrace matter that was expressly disclaimed in the original, or impliedly excluded by the original descriptions and limitations; the inventor is bound by statements and limitations in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (§680): "The nature of the subject-matter which the inventor intended and attempted to describe and claim in his original specifications may be further indicated by the limitations which he has imposed ... in consequence of these his re-issue may be confined within narrower boundaries than the character of his invention would otherwise require." Cases cited: Beecher Mfg. Co. v. Atwater Mfg. Co., Avery v. etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and limitations in original are binding; omissions may void re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements in the original patent (including professed dispensations or limitations) are binding upon the patentee and omission of limitations in the re-issue that enlarge the invention are invalid; re-issue cannot enlarge invention by omitting words in original claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "The statements of an inventor in his original Claim and specifications are binding upon him ... That a re-issue enlarging the invention by omitting words found in the original Claim is invalid," with cases Matthews v. Iron Clad Mfg. Co., James v. Campbell, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original identification with single form bars claiming other forms in re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original identifies the invention with one form only, the re-issue cannot claim other forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That if the original identifies the invention with one form the re-issue cannot claim other forms, see Steam Gauge & Lantern Co. v. Miller and cases cited."

rubrics_metrics.name: Original limiting to certain qualities/uses bars re-issue to other qualities/uses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original limits the invention to matter possessing certain qualities or capabilities for certain uses, the re-issue can claim no other qualities or uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "That if the original limits the invention to matter possessing certain qualities or capabilities for certain uses, the re-issue can claim no other qualities or uses," with cases Doane v. Wellington Mfg. Co. v. Smith, Ex parte Bragg, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot convert erroneous causal statements into new claimed causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the original attributes effects to erroneous causes, the patentee's subsequent discovery of the true causes cannot be made available by re-issue to claim the newly discovered causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "Where he mistakes the nature of his invention, and in the original specification attributes the effects which it produces to erroneous causes, his subsequent discovery of the true causes cannot be made available to him by a re-issue..." Cases: Eames v. Andrews, Andrews v. Hovey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority among multiple patents: only patent that claimed matter may re-issue for it
rubrics_metrics.description: When the inventor procured two separate patents and has claimed the matter in but one of them, only that patent can re-issue to embrace it; if claimed in neither, it can be covered by a re-issue of the earliest alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: discussion in §680: if inventor filed multiple patents, the right to re-issue for matter depends on which patent originally claimed it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of invention determined by comparing specifications (and drawings/models)
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity of the invention claimed in the re-issue with that attempted to be covered in the original is ascertained, in most cases, by a simple comparison of their respective specifications; where drawings/models are involved they are the proper objects of comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (§681): "The identity ... is ascertained ... by a simple comparison of their respective specifications ... Where the invention is of a nature admitting of illustration by drawings or models, this is the only investigation which can be made." Cases: Ex parte Seibert, Ex parte Baldwin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrinsic evidence only to explain technical terms or apply descriptions to subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Extrinsic evidence is not admissible except to explain the meaning of technical terms or to apply the language of the description to its proper subject-matter; generally identity is decided from the patents themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "Extrinsic evidence is not admissible except to explain the meaning of technical terms, or to apply the language of the Description to its proper subject-matter." Cases: Seymour v. Osborne; Heald v. Rice; Union Paper Collar Co. v. Van Deusen (parol evidence not admissible to enlarge scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue presumed same invention as original until contrary appears
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issued patent is presumed to be for the same invention as the original until the contrary appears; differences in descriptions and claims are immaterial if inventions are the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "It is presumed that it is for the same invention as the original until the contrary appears ... Differences in the Description and the Claims are not material, provided the inventions are the same." Cited cases and discussion of burden of proof follow §681 and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: If identity not apparent on face, re-issue may be sustained; if apparent difference, re-issue void
rubrics_metrics.description: If on the face of the two specifications it is apparent that the re-issue claims a substantially distinct invention, the re-issue is void; if diversity is not apparent, the re-issue will be sustained as to this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "If on the face of the two specifications ... it is apparent that the invention claimed in the re-issue is substantially distinct ... the re-issue is void. If the diversity is not apparent, the re-issue ... will be sustained."

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and model may be inspected; model presumptions and lost-model rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings and model may be inspected to determine identity; if a feature claimed in re-issue is absent from specification/drawings, the model will be presumed to contain it unless produced; where model lost, changes in drawings only on most conclusive evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "Drawings and model originally filed may be examined ... a dilapidated model may be aided by evidence ... when a feature claimed in the re-issue is absent ... the model will be presumed to contain it unless the model is produced. Where the model is lost ... no change can be permitted ... except upon the most conclusive evidence." Cases: Johnsen v. Beard; Hendy v. Golden State & Miners' Iron Works; Flower v. Detroit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of re-issue application files may resolve doubts about scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In any doubt as to the scope of the re-issue specification, the files of the re-issue application may be resorted to for its solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "In any doubt as to the scope of the re-issue specification the files of the re-issue application may be resorted to for its solution."
